q: 1. Reciprocal leveling eliminates .............
options: collimation and curvature error fully and refraction error pertly
explain: By taking observations from both ends of a line, reciprocal leveling cancels out errors due to earth's curvature, atmospheric refraction (assuming it's constant), and imperfect adjustment of the line of collimation.

q: 2. A level surface to which elevation of different points are referred to, is known as:
explain: A datum is the reference level surface to which the elevations of all other points in a survey are referred.

q: 3. A relatively permanent point of reference whose elevation is known as:
explain: As defined earlier, a bench mark is a relatively permanent point of reference whose elevation is already known.

q: 4. How many types of bench mark are there?
explain: As per this text, bench marks are classified into two main types.

q: 5. A fixed point of reference of known elevation is called .............
explain: A Bench Mark (BM) is a permanent or semi-permanent point of known elevation used as a reference for leveling.

q: 6. An imaginary line tangent to the longitudinal curve of the bubble tube at its middle points is called .............
explain: The axis of the level tube is the tangent to the inner surface of the bubble tube at its midpoint.

q: 7. The sensitivity of bubble tube can be increased by .............
options: decreasing the radius of curvature of tube
explain: Sensitivity increases with an increase in the internal diameter and the radius of curvature, and with a decrease in liquid viscosity.

q: 8. With the rise of temperature, the sensitivity of bubble tube .............
explain: When temperature rises, the liquid in the tube expands, causing the bubble length to decrease, which reduces the sensitivity of the tube.

q: 9. Refraction correction .............
options: has no effect on the curvature correction
explain: The refraction correction is negative (subtracts from staff reading) and the curvature correction is positive; since refraction is about 1/7 of curvature, it partially offsets it.

q: 10. While doing leveling in undulating terrain, it is preferable to set level on .............
explain: Setting the level on a side slope provides a clearer line of sight for both uphill and downhill points in hilly terrain.

q: 11. A leveling station is a place where .............
options: both B.S. and F.S. are taken
explain: In leveling terminology, a 'station' refers specifically to the location where the leveling staff is held, not where the instrument is placed.

q: 12. The telescope of a dumpy level .............
options: is rigidly fixed to the leveling head
can be tilted in a vertical plane
can be taken out of its supports and reversed
permits interchange of eye piece and object glass
explain: In a dumpy level, the telescope is rigidly fixed to its supports and cannot be rotated about its longitudinal axis or tilted vertically.

q: 13. The function of levelling head is
options: to attach the theodolite to the tripod
to provide a bearing for the outer hollow spindle
to provide a mean of levelling the instrument
explain: The leveling head serves as the interface between the tripod and the instrument, supporting the vertical axis and housing the leveling mechanism.

q: 14. Bench marks are fixed by
explain: Bench marks are established with high accuracy using ordinary spirit levelling, which provides the precision required for a permanent reference elevation point.

q: 15. The method of finding out the difference in elevation between two points for eliminating the effect of curvature and refraction is
explain: Reciprocal leveling involves taking sights from both ends of a line (e.g., across a river) to cancel out errors from earth curvature, atmospheric refraction, and instrument adjustment.

q: 16. A straight line tangential to the longitudinal curve of the level tube at its center, is known as
explain: The bubble line (or axis of the level tube) is the tangent to the inner surface of the tube at its midpoint.

q: 17. Profile leveling is usually done for determining .............
explain: Profile leveling (longitudinal leveling) is performed to find the elevations of points at known distances along a fixed line, such as a road or railway centerline.

q: 18. Parallax may be eliminated by
explain: You must first focus the eyepiece to see the crosshairs clearly, then focus the objective to bring the image onto the crosshair plane.

q: 19. Pick up the odd instrument .............
explain: Prismatic compasses, theodolites, and sextants are primarily used to measure angles. A dumpy level is used specifically for measuring vertical differences in elevation (leveling).

q: 20. In an adjusted level, when the bubble is central, the axis of the bubble tube becomes parallel to
explain: For an instrument to be in perfect adjustment, the axis of the bubble tube must be parallel to the line of collimation so that the line of sight is horizontal when the bubble is centered.

q: 21. Height of instrument method of leveling is
options: more accurate than rise and fall method
less accurate than rise and fall method
quicker and less tedious for large number of intermediate sights
explain: The HI (Height of Collimation) method is faster for projects with many intermediate sights (like longitudinal sections) because it requires fewer calculations than the Rise and Fall method.

q: 22. A back sight indicates the ............ of the instrument.
explain: A back sight is the first reading taken after the instrument is set up on a new station, taken on a point of known elevation.

q: 23. Sensitiveness of a level tube is designated by
options: length of bubble of level tube
explain: Sensitivity increases with the radius of curvature of the internal surface of the tube; a larger radius means a more sensitive bubble.

q: 24. Dumpy level is most suitable when
options: the instrument is to be shifted frequently
fly leveling is being done over long distance
many readings are to be taken from a single setting
explain: The Dumpy level is sturdy and maintains its adjustment well, making it ideal for taking numerous intermediate sights from a single position.

q: 25. A change point is
options: intermediate station where fs and bs taken
station after which instrument is shifted
explain: A change point (CP) is a stable point on which both a Foresight (to close the current setup) and a Backsight (to start the next setup) are taken.

q: 26. Benchmark is established by
explain: Spirit leveling (using a level and staff) is the most precise method for determining elevations and establishing Bench Marks.

q: 27. Ten readings were recorded... If the instrument was shifted after 2nd and 6th readings, then the fore sights are
explain: Foresights are the last readings before shifting (2nd and 6th) and the very last reading of the entire operation (10th).

q: 28. The following readings were taken on a uniformly sloping ground... Hence difference in elevation between first and last station is
explain: The difference in elevation is the sum of Backsights minus the sum of Foresights. Calculation based on the sequence provided in the text leads to a 3.000m fall.

q: 29. Due to curvature of earth the object
explain: The earth's curvature causes a level line to drop away from a horizontal line of sight, making distant objects appear higher than their true elevation relative to the observer.

q: 30. Correction for curvature for a distance of 1 km =
explain: The formula for curvature correction is $C_c = 0.0785 D^2$. For $D=1$ km, $C_c = 0.0785$ meters.

q: 31. Correction for refraction for a distance of 1 km =
explain: The formula for refraction correction is $C_r = 0.0112 D^2$. For $D=1$ km, $C_r = 0.0112$ meters.

q: 32. In profile leveling, staff readings on neighbouring pegs 20 m apart are 1.200 and 1.000... proposed road had a
explain: Difference in level = $1.200 - 1.000 = 0.200$ (Fall). Gradient = $0.2 / 20 = 1 / 100$ (Falling).

q: 33. An example for instrument error in leveling is
explain: Collimation error occurs when the line of sight is not perfectly horizontal when the bubble is centered, which is a direct flaw in the instrument's adjustment.

q: 34. When the temperature rises, length of bubble
explain: As temperature increases, the liquid in the level tube expands, which causes the vapor bubble to contract and become shorter.

q: 35. Sensitiveness of bubble tube can be increased by
options: reducing internal radius of the tube
explain: Increasing the diameter or the radius of curvature of the tube allows the bubble to move more significantly for smaller changes in inclination.

q: 36. Sensitiveness of Bubble tube
explain: This formula relates the number of divisions moved ($n$) and the distance ($D$) to the sensitivity value.

q: 37. Permanent adjustments of a level are .............
explain: For a dumpy level, the two permanent adjustments are making the axis of the bubble tube perpendicular to the vertical axis and making the line of collimation parallel to the axis of the bubble tube.

q: 38. Number of subdivisions per metre length of a leveling staff is .............
explain: A standard metric leveling staff has a least count of 5mm (0.005m). Therefore, there are 1/0.005 = 200 subdivisions per meter.

q: 39. The power of a telescope to form distinguishable images of objects separated by small angular distance is called its .............
explain: Resolving power is the ability of the telescope to separate and distinguish two closely spaced objects as distinct images.

q: 40. The angle of field of the telescope .............
options: is independent of the size of the object glass
increases as the size of the eye piece increases
decreases as the distance between eye piece and object increases
explain: The field of view depends primarily on the eyepiece and the magnification, not the size of the objective (object glass), which mainly affects brightness.

q: 41. The line of collimation method of reduction of levels, does not provide a check on .............
explain: Unlike the Rise and Fall method, the Height of Instrument (Collimation) method does not have a built-in arithmetic check for intermediate sights.

q: 42. During leveling if back sight is more than foresight .............
options: the forward staff is at lower point
the back staff is at lower point
the difference in level, cannot be ascertained
explain: If the foresight reading is smaller than the back sight reading, the ground has risen. Therefore, the forward staff is at a higher elevation, making the back staff point lower.

q: 43. The rise and fall method of reduction of levels, provides a check on .............
explain: The Rise and Fall method is more rigorous because it includes a check on the calculation of reduced levels for intermediate sights, unlike the Height of Instrument method.

q: 44. Resolving power of a telescope depends on .............
options: the pupil aperture of the eye
the diameter of the object glass
explain: Resolving power is influenced by the diffraction limit (determined by the objective diameter) and the observer's eye capability.

q: 45. The longitudinal section of the surface of bubble tube is .............
explain: The inner surface of a bubble tube is ground to a circular arc of a large radius so that the bubble moves linearly with respect to the tilt angle.

q: 46. The bubble tube is nearly filled with .............
options: a liquid which is very mobile
a liquid having low freezing point
explain: Liquids like synthetic alcohol or ether are used because they move quickly (low viscosity/mobile) and won't freeze in cold conditions.

q: 47. The radius of curvature of the bubble tube is generally kept .............
explain: A large radius (like 100m) is required to make the bubble sensitive to very small changes in inclination.

q: 48. In the double application of principle of reversion, the apparent error is .............
explain: In testing adjustments via reversion, the displacement between the two positions is twice the actual error.

q: 49. A level line is .............
options: line parallel to the mean spheriodal surface of earth
line passing through the centers of cross hairs and the center of eye piece
line passing through the objective lens and the eye piece of a dumpy or tilting level
explain: A level line is a curved line that is equidistant from the center of the earth at every point.

q: 50. The following sights are taken on the turning point .............
explain: At a change point (CP), a Foresight is taken to determine its elevation, and then a Backsight is taken to continue the leveling from that new height.
